title: Admissions, denials, and lack of knowledge
shortTitle: Admissions, denials, and lack of knowledge
summary: An answer responds to the complaint’s allegations by admitting them, denying them, or properly stating insufficient knowledge. Those responses define what remains disputed.
notes: A defective answer can require correction. The consequences of an admission and permission to amend it depend on the procedural setting, as Beeck illustrates.

sections.Meaning: An answer responds to the complaint’s allegations by admitting them, denying them, or properly stating insufficient knowledge. Those responses define what remains disputed.
sections.How to work through the question: Read each allegation fairly and respond to its substance. A party cannot evade a factual allegation merely by calling it a legal conclusion, and a claimed lack of knowledge must be appropriate to the information the party has.
